h1: The 6 Best Bagged Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six bagged upright and canister vacuums compared on filtration, tools, weight and pet-friendly disposal for 2026.
summary: The Kenmore 81414 400 Series is our top bagged vacuum for households that want HEPA filtration and a full tool kit. The Kenmore 81214 gives a similar HEPA and two-motor setup for less, the Oreck Commercial XL is the lightweight upright for durability, and the Eureka 3670H is the cheapest way into a canister.
intro: Bagged vacuums are making a quiet comeback because the bag does something a bin cannot: it seals dust inside until you throw it away. The buying mistake is assuming all bags are equal. Whether a machine adds HEPA filtration and how many tools come in the box matter far more than the brand name on the shell.

We ranked six bagged models on paper using their spec sheets and owner reports, comparing filtration, tools, body type, weight and price bracket. Prices are given as buckets because retailers change them often.

products.name: Kenmore 81414 400 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum with Extended Telescoping Wand, HEPA, Retractable Cord, and 4 Cleaning Tools
products.verdict: The most complete bagged canister in this group.
products.description:
This canister combines HEPA filtration, an extended telescoping wand, a retractable cord and four cleaning tools. It is priced at $200-500, the top bracket here.

It wins because the tool count and wand reach suit stairs, upholstery and ceiling corners without buying extras. The 81214 below shares HEPA but ships with fewer tools and costs less.

Best for households with pets and mixed floors that want one machine to do everything. If your home is mostly carpet, an upright from the Kenmore Intuition line may suit better.
products.idealFor: Pet households with mixed floors and stairs.

products.name: Kenmore 81214 200 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum with HEPA, 2 Motor System, and 3 Cleaning Tools
products.verdict: HEPA and a two-motor design without the premium price.
products.description:
A bagged canister with HEPA filtration, a 2-motor system and three cleaning tools, listed in the $100-200 range.

Compared with the 400 Series above, you lose one tool and the extended wand, but you keep the filtration and the dual motor. That makes it the better deal for most buyers.

Choose it if you want HEPA and strong suction on a moderate budget. Those who clean tall spaces may miss the telescoping reach.

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL Vacuum Cleaner, Bagged Upright Vac, Lightweight
products.verdict: A light, durable upright for people who dislike lugging a canister.
products.description:
The Commercial XL is a lightweight bagged upright with commercial-grade construction. It runs $100-200.

The spec sheet lists no HEPA claim or tool kit, which is why it trails the two Kenmore canisters. In exchange, an upright with a light body is easier to push around a whole floor.

Buy it for quick, regular cleaning of carpets and hard floors where durability counts. Do not expect attachments for upholstery.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum with Hair Eliminator Brushroll
products.verdict: Targets the tangled brushroll that ruins other uprights.
products.description:
This upright pairs a bagged body with a Hair Eliminator brushroll, which is built to reduce hair wrapping around the roller. It lands in the $100-200 bracket.

The brushroll is what separates it from the plainer Intuition below, and it beats the Lift-Up model for homes with long hair or pets.

Pick it if tangles are your pet peeve. The listing shows no HEPA or tool details.
products.idealFor: Homes with long hair or shedding pets.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum Lift-Up Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: An upright that lifts off for stairs, no canister needed.
products.description:
The Lift-Up design lets you detach the cleaning section from the upright body, handy for stairs and upholstery. It is a bagged upright in the $100-200 bracket.

It sits behind the Hair Eliminator because stairs are a narrower use than tangles, but it solves a real gap in uprights.

A fit for multi-level carpeted homes. Check the listing for the wand length before you rely on it for tall dusting.

products.name: Eureka Bagged Canister Vacuum Cleaner, 3670H
products.verdict: Canister reach for the least money here.
products.description:
A bagged canister that includes replacement bags, priced at $50-100, the lowest bracket in this ranking.

It finishes last because the listing gives no filtration or tool details, so you are buying the form factor and the cheap entry.

Good for apartments or a second-floor vacuum that rarely gets heavy use. Expect fewer features than the Kenmore canisters.

methodology.title: Filtration
methodology.description: Whether HEPA is listed and how well dust stays sealed in the bag.

methodology.title: Tools and reach
methodology.description: The number of attachments and wand length for stairs and upholstery.

methodology.title: Body style
methodology.description: Upright versus canister and how each handles carpet, floors and weight.

whatMatters.detail: A HEPA filter traps very fine particles that ordinary filters release back into the air. It matters most for allergy sufferers and pet owners. Look for the word HEPA in the title or bullets, not a vague claim of allergen filtering.
Uprights are fast on carpet and store upright. Canisters reach stairs, furniture and ceilings more easily. Think about your floors and storage before buying.
A bagged vacuum needs bags that fit its model. Check that replacements are easy to buy and compare costs. A listing that includes spare bags saves an early reorder.
Hair wraps around plain brushrolls and forces you to cut it free. A Hair Eliminator style design reduces that. Check the product title for it if you have long hair or pets.
Crevice tools, dusting brushes and upholstery heads are what make a canister useful beyond floors. Count the tools in the title or bullets before you buy.

howToChoose.intro: Match the body style to what you clean most.

cards.label: Upright
cards.text: Faster on large carpeted areas and stores simply. The Oreck Commercial XL and the two Kenmore Intuition uprights belong here.

cards.label: Canister
cards.text: Better on stairs, furniture and bare floors. The Kenmore 81414, Kenmore 81214 and Eureka 3670H belong here.

howToChoose.note: Most mixed-floor homes should default to a canister.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: HEPA filtration, a tangle-resistant brushroll and sealed bag disposal.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Kenmore 81414 and 81214 pair HEPA with a bagged design, and the Intuition Hair Eliminator targets tangles.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want HEPA and a full tool kit; the Kenmore 81414 400 Series covers both.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean occasionally; the Eureka 3670H or Oreck Commercial XL is enough.

faq.q: Are bagged vacuums better than bagless?
faq.a: They seal dust inside until disposal, which is cleaner for allergies. The tradeoff is buying bags.

faq.q: Do all of these use HEPA?
faq.a: Only the Kenmore 81414 and 81214 list HEPA. The others do not claim it.

faq.q: How often should I change the bag?
faq.a: Change it when it is roughly full, since a packed bag cuts airflow. Many owners swap it when suction drops.

faq.q: Is an upright or canister better for stairs?
faq.a: A canister or the Kenmore Intuition Lift-Up works best on stairs.
No. Bags are model-specific, so confirm the style number before you order.

faq.q: Is the Eureka 3670H enough for a pet home?
faq.a: Likely for light use, but the Kenmore canisters offer HEPA and more tools.

finalTake: The Kenmore 81414 400 Series is the best bagged vacuum here for homes that want everything in one canister. The 81214 is the smarter buy for most budgets, and the Oreck is the upright to choose for simple carpet cleaning.
